name: Annual Review & Next-Year Plan
description: For board and leadership annual reviews: editorial serif conclusions, deep-navy authority, red strategic emphasis, objective scorecards, parallel year timelines, candid lessons, and capital-linked priorities.
style_guide:
# Annual Review & Next-Year Plan

## Design intent

Create a board- and leadership-ready annual review that connects the year just closed to the operating choices for the year ahead. The visual language combines a deep-navy executive cover, editorial serif claims, cool-white analytical pages, disciplined red emphasis, restrained green outcome coding, parallel annual timelines, and capital-linked strategic priorities. It should feel like a well-edited CEO or CFO report translated into presentation form: candid, durable, and specific about what was promised, what happened, why, and what changes next.

Each page should carry one annual conclusion and make the supporting evidence, causal explanation, owner, and next-year consequence visible. Preserve the visual grammar shown by the previews, but never copy their company, people, financials, customers, product names, objectives, dates, or plan assumptions. Preview images are UI-only references; this written guide is the complete authoring authority.

## Core visual signature

- Use a dark institutional cover and sparse dark summary bands to establish authority; keep most analytical pages white or cool gray.
- Pair a high-contrast editorial serif for annual claims, strategic objectives, hero metrics, and priority statements with a neutral sans-serif for evidence and a tracked monospaced face for metadata.
- Use Strategic red for the active year, decisive emphasis, challenge, record period, priority rail, or key change. Use Outcome green only for met or exceeded results.
- Use large, simple exhibits: objective tables, annual bar comparisons, four operating KPI cards, synchronized timelines, symmetric challenge/lesson rows, and a focused next-year priority stack.
- Make the bridge from challenge to lesson to strategic priority explicit. The plan should respond to what the review actually learned.
- Keep the style editorial and evidence-led. Avoid dashboard decoration, stock photography, glossy annual-report effects, and celebratory clutter.

## Canvas, grid, and spacing

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` canvas in a 16:9 ratio.
- Keep `64 px` left and right safe margins and `34–44 px` top and bottom safe margins. No source, target, owner, or qualification may be clipped.
- Use a 12-column grid with `18–22 px` gutters. Align title starts, table columns, KPI cards, timeline quarters, priority rails, and footer notes to shared grid lines.
- Place a compact page metadata line at the top with page number and section at left and company, period, or review identity at right. Use a one-pixel rule beneath.
- Reserve `98–124 px` for title and subtitle on body pages, followed by `26–38 px` before the main exhibit.
- Use `24–30 px` between major panels, `14–20 px` between related modules, and `8–12 px` between a label and value.
- The cover uses generous vertical breathing room, a subtle grid, and a lower KPI and presenter field. It should not resemble a dense title page.
- Keep a quiet `22–28 px` footer zone for scoring rules, sources, alignment notes, or checkpoint cadence.

## Color system

### Foundation colors

- Institutional navy: `#0F172A`. Use for the cover canvas, primary headlines, table headers, dark summary bands, the annual aspiration panel, customer timeline identity, and decisive conclusions.
- Stage white: `#FFFFFF`. Use as the dominant analytical canvas and primary reverse text on Institutional navy.
- Cool report canvas: `#F8FAFC`. Use for alternating table rows, KPI cards, lessons, priority cards, and analytical grouping.
- Structural gray: `#CBD5E1`. Use for prior-year bars, axes, borders, rules, and inactive comparisons.
- Primary slate: `#64748B`. Use for body copy, chart labels, supporting descriptions, and metadata.
- Quiet reverse slate: `#94A3B8`. Use for supporting copy, labels, and metadata on Institutional navy.

### Strategic and outcome colors

- Strategic red: `#DC2626`. Use for the active or record period, short cover rail, missed objective, challenge column, priority rail, current change, and key forward target.
- Red wash: `#FEF2F2`. Use for challenge cards, missed-objective rows, and qualified downside contexts.
- Outcome green: `#15803D`. Use for met or exceeded objectives, verified improvement, positive variance, and achieved outcome rails.
- Green wash: `#DCFCE7`. Use for compact met/exceeded badges and low-intensity positive status.
- Product blue: `#1D4ED8`. Use for the product track and only for product-specific annual milestones or one supporting series.
- Team teal: `#0F766E`. Use for the team track and only for people or organization milestones.

### Color discipline

- Institutional navy, Stage white, and Strategic red define the annual-report identity. Green, Product blue, and Team teal are semantic secondary colors.
- Red may mean the active year or strategic emphasis in charts and headings, and a challenge or miss in status contexts. The local label must make its meaning explicit.
- Use Green only for grounded positive outcomes. Do not make every favorable number green on a page where Red already carries the active-year series.
- Product blue and Team teal remain tied to their tracks. Do not recycle them for unrelated categories.
- Use flat fills. The cover may use an extremely subtle low-contrast grid, but no gradient, glow, texture, or shadow.
- Never rely on color alone. Pair every series, status, track, and priority with a direct label.

## Typography

- Display serif: `Georgia`, with `Times New Roman` or another readable editorial serif as fallback. Use it for the cover title, body-page claims, objective statements, hero values, challenge/lesson headlines, and priority outcomes.
- Evidence sans-serif: `Inter`, with `Arial`, `Helvetica Neue`, or a compatible system sans-serif as fallback. Use it for subtitles, tables, chart labels, explanations, owners, and footnotes.
- Metadata face: `IBM Plex Mono`, with `Consolas` or `Courier New` as fallback. Use it for page codes, periods, sources, units, track labels, and small status metadata.
- For CJK output, use an established CJK serif for display claims and a common CJK sans-serif for evidence. Use monospaced CJK only for short metadata. Preserve contrast and line length rather than forcing Latin tracking.
- Cover title: `48–62 px`, serif, weight `700`, line-height `1.02–1.08`, Stage white. Keep to two or three deliberate lines.
- Body-page title: `34–44 px`, serif, weight `700`, line-height `1.05–1.13`, Institutional navy.
- Hero metric or aspiration: `36–52 px`, serif, weight `700`, using tabular numerals where available.
- Module title: `18–23 px`, serif or bold sans-serif according to density. Use serif for strategic statements and sans-serif for analytical labels.
- Body copy: `12–15 px`, sans-serif, weight `400–500`, line-height `1.4–1.55`.
- Table headers, track labels, page codes, sources, and units: `8–11 px`, metadata face, weight `500–700`, uppercase when appropriate, letter-spacing `1.3–2.3 px`.
- Do not use the serif for dense rationale columns or long paragraphs. Do not shrink evidence to preserve every possible detail.

## Cover and executive framing

- Use a full Institutional-navy canvas with a very faint large-cell grid. Add a thin upper metadata rule and a short Strategic-red title rail.
- Place the fiscal year and review/plan scope above a large editorial title. Leave meaningful open space around it.
- Use one two-line framing sentence below the title. Bold only the operating promise or central thesis.
- Add a four-column KPI strip for the most decision-relevant full-year outcomes. Each KPI includes label, value, and one compact prior-period or plan comparison.
- End with presenter, company, forum, date, version, and close status aligned along the lower grid.
- Do not add photography, company-history copy, a large logo, or an agenda list to the cover. The annual thesis and evidence establish authority.

## Tables, cards, and evidence structures

- Use square or nearly square corners: `0–2 px` radius. Components use thin borders or colored rails and no drop shadows.
- Objective tables use an Institutional-navy header, alternating Stage-white and Cool-report rows, a colored left status rail, large serif objective and actual values, and a one-line rationale.
- KPI cards use Cool report canvas, a thin Outcome-green rail when the metric is verified positive, and one short causal note. Avoid stuffing several unrelated KPIs into one card.
- Dark summary bands use Institutional navy, Stage-white claim typography, a short Strategic-red rail, and one equation or evidence line.
- Challenge cards use Red wash and a Strategic-red left rail. Lesson cards use Cool report canvas and an Institutional-navy left rail. Keep the paired rows symmetric.
- Priority cards use Cool report canvas, a Strategic-red left rail, a large serif outcome statement, and a lower evidence row for owner, annual outcome, leading indicator, and capital.
- Status badges remain small, square, and text-labeled: Exceeded, Met, Missed, or the appropriate localized terms.

## Charts, annual comparisons, and timelines

- Prefer quarterly grouped bars, annual KPI cards, full-year objective tables, synchronized 12-month timelines, and plan-priority stacks.
- Use Structural gray for the prior year, Institutional navy for completed current-year quarters, and Strategic red for the active, record, or decisive current period.
- Use a zero baseline for revenue and financial bars. Direct-label the quarterly values and total.
- Every financial chart must state currency, scale, fiscal/calendar basis, reporting period, actual/estimate/forecast status, and source.
- A dark annual conclusion band may combine growth and profitability into one defined rule or threshold. State the formula and do not substitute a fashionable metric without explaining it.
- Parallel timelines share the same quarter axis. Give each track a colored identity panel, one milestone per quarter at most, and an evidence or implication line beneath each marker.
- Customer, product, and team events should be plotted on the same time axis only when their timing relationship supports a real conclusion. Do not imply causation solely through visual proximity.
- Plan priorities require a lagging annual outcome, a 90-day or other near-term leading indicator, owner, capital or resource allocation, and the lesson they address.

## Adaptable composition families

These are composition tendencies, not executable templates, a mandatory sequence, or permission to reuse preview content. Choose the structure that best serves the annual argument.

- Cover and annual thesis: use the full navy cover, editorial title, four full-year KPIs, presenter and forum metadata, and one sentence connecting review to plan.
- Strategic-objective review: use an owner-based table of four to six objectives with original target, actual, status, and one-line rationale. Publish the scoring rule.
- Financial and operating results: place one dominant quarterly or annual chart on the left and four operating KPI cards on the right. Close with one dark band for the integrated annual conclusion.
- Customer, product, and team milestones: use synchronized quarterly timelines with distinct Institutional-navy, Product-blue, and Team-teal track identities. End with an alignment or sequencing observation.
- Challenges and lessons: use symmetric left/right columns. Each left challenge states what was underestimated and its evidence; the matching right lesson states the specific operating change for next year.
- Next-year strategic priorities: place a dark aspiration and target panel on the left and three priority cards on the right. Every priority carries a single owner, outcome, leading indicator, capital, and linkage to a lesson.
- Portfolio review alternative: use business-unit or product rows with revenue, margin, strategic role, capital employed, and a clear invest/hold/fix/exit decision.
- Capital allocation alternative: use a funding bridge, three to five investment priorities, expected outcomes, decision gates, and downside or reallocation triggers.
- Organization plan alternative: use capability gaps, leadership changes, headcount or productivity assumptions, critical roles, and organizational milestones tied to the strategy.

## Annual narrative and planning discipline

- Begin with the original commitments, not only the results that are convenient to celebrate.
- Explain the most material positive and negative variances through evidence-backed mechanisms. Avoid attributing every outcome to execution quality alone.
- Connect events across the year only when timing, evidence, and business logic support the relationship.
- Translate every challenge into a concrete lesson and every lesson into a plan change, owner, metric, resource, and checkpoint.
- Limit the next-year plan to three to five true enterprise priorities. Ordinary departmental work belongs in supporting operating plans.
- Make the difference between aspiration, board-approved plan, budget, forecast, target, and stretch explicit.
- State what will not be funded or pursued when the plan makes a real resource tradeoff.

## Content truth and reporting restrictions

- Treat every preview company, person, metric, objective, customer, product, date, target, challenge, lesson, and capital amount as fictional reference content. Never reuse it unless independently grounded in the current Workspace.
- Never invent revenue, growth, margin, cash, retention, customer, product, reliability, people, hiring, engagement, pipeline, or plan figures.
- Distinguish audited, closed, preliminary, management estimate, forecast, plan, budget, target, stretch, and aspiration. Do not present a draft plan as an approved commitment.
- State fiscal-year boundaries, reporting currency, consolidation scope, constant-currency treatment where relevant, and the data-lock date.
- Objective status must follow the published rule. Do not retroactively rewrite original targets or judge performance using a different denominator.
- A one-line rationale needs evidence. Separate verified causal drivers from management interpretation or hypothesis.
- Customer, product, compliance, security, reliability, and people claims must use correct definitions and status. A launch, beta, GA, certification, audit, signed customer, reference, and recognized revenue are not interchangeable.
- Plan outcomes and capital allocations need assumptions, owner, time horizon, checkpoints, and downside triggers. Do not fabricate precision to fill priority fields.
- Board, employee, customer, and partner confidentiality must be respected. Use anonymization or aggregation where required.
- If a fact or assumption is missing, omit it, label it preliminary or `TBD`, show an explicit range, or state the decision still required.

## Allowed variation

- Preserve the dark executive cover, light analytical body, editorial serif claims, sans-serif evidence, Strategic-red emphasis, square components, and review-to-plan narrative.
- Product blue and Team teal may change to other restrained track colors if the actual categories differ, but Institutional navy and Strategic red remain dominant.
- The deck may serve a company, division, nonprofit, program, or portfolio. Adapt objective types and planning vocabulary without weakening the evidence and ownership requirements.
- Use fewer or more than three timelines only when each remains wide enough for readable quarterly milestones.
- Adapt capitalization, tracking, date formats, currency formats, and line breaks to the confirmed output language. Preserve the serif/sans contrast rather than literal English layouts.

## Avoid

- Do not reproduce preview facts, people, companies, metrics, objectives, challenges, priorities, or capital plans. Transfer the annual-review grammar only.
- Do not use glossy annual-report photography, celebratory collages, generic office imagery, gradients, glassmorphism, 3D charts, gauges, or rounded SaaS cards.
- Do not turn every favorable value green or every current-year value red without an explicit local meaning.
- Do not show only achievements. A credible annual review includes misses, challenges, and changes in operating behavior.
- Do not pair a challenge with a vague lesson such as communicate more or execute better. Specify the process, owner, metric, and timing change.
- Do not list more than six strategic objectives, four operating KPI cards, four challenge/lesson pairs, or five enterprise priorities on one main page.
- Do not imply causation through coincident timelines without evidence.
- Do not hide plan assumptions, resource requirements, downside cases, unresolved decisions, or approval status in unreadable footnotes.
